text.p: Banco Ambrosiano Veneto said on Wednesday it approved a merger with Cariplo, creating Italy's biggest banking group in terms of number of branches, gross operating profit and capacity to generate revenue.

Ambroveneto said in a statement it would make a capital increase of around 6.5 trillion lire ($3.6 billion) to fund the 100 percent purchase of Cassa di Risparmio delle Provincie Lombarde (Cariplo). This will be via a two-for-one share and warrant issue with a price range for ordinary shares of between 2,800 and 3,400 lire and 1,800 and 2,200 lire for savings shares.
It said it would also issue two five-year convertible bond issues for a total of around 1.074 trillion lire.
Ambroveneto said the new private banking group would be the country's second biggest in terms of assets, deposits and loans, after Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino.
The new group will have a total of 1,822 branches, or a national market share of 7.5 percent, well ahead of rivals.
It said the integration between the two banking groups in four phases should be completed by June 30, 1998.
Ambroveneto said the four phases would be as follows:

1. the transfer from Cariplo bank of certain assets like non-banking holdings and real estate, for a total value not less than 1.68 trillion lire, to a company to be controlled by Cariplo's foundation.

2. The hiving off from the current Banco Ambrosiano Veneto of part of the banking company in a new 100 percent-controlled company. Banco Ambrosiano Veneto will thus have the role of parent company of the new banking group.

3. The foundation which currently controls Cariplo will transfer to the new parent company 100 percent of Cariplo for a value equal to the total of Cariplo net assets at end-1996 less the net book value on the same date of the assets transfer.
4. Cariplo's foundation will hold a significant stake of the capital of the new parent company and will be a member of the shareholders' syndicate.
Ambroveneto said an AGM and EGM will meet on September 30 to examine the above mentioned financial plan.
